instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: How Much Do You Know?
cards.instruction: Probe for what others know while revealing as little as possible.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's separate what you saw from what you heard. Which part of the party do you know about?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The cake went over the balcony. Was that before you left?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's a question about timing, not a fact. Who gave you a time?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Nobody. Your brother says there's a video.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Have you watched it? 'Someone has a video' is not yet a witness statement.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: What exactly did the manager say about the missing keys? Her words, please, not a reconstruction.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They might be in the drain. You locked up, didn't you?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: 'Might' isn't a location. Is she asking everyone who locked up, or specifically asking about me?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Just you. Someone saw you outside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Doing what? Please don't turn 'outside' into 'dropped the keys.' What did the witness actually report?

cards.title: Join Me
cards.instruction: Recruit someone into a secret plan.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We need twenty minutes to hide Mum's cake. Ask about her pastry; 'come here, it's a surprise' is not a distraction.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I only said that last year.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And she found the cake. This time, ask her to show you how she crimps the edge.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She'll make me bake a whole pie.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Ask about one edge. I'll give you a strip of pastry; we need a demonstration, not a second birthday meal.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Take Denise for coffee while I put up the leaving-party decorations. Don't say 'we need you out of the office.'

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She won't go until this spreadsheet balances.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've added the totals row twice. Remove the second one and tell her the figures are ready.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then she'll want to stay and check them herself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Send her the corrected copy to read over coffee. The coffee is the invitation; the word 'distraction' must remain inside your head.

cards.title: You First
cards.instruction: Coax someone else into breaking a rule before you do.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The rooftop light is right for the dress. Through the staff-only door first, please; I'll follow with the camera.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm the bride. They'll notice me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Being noticed is rather the point of a bridal portrait. Chin up, and don't bunch the train in your hands.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then walk beside me and carry it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The train needs the doorway to itself. I'll hold the end; you go through first, slowly, before I bring the camera in.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Try one grape from the middle of the bunch. The ripest-looking one won't tell us whether the rest are sour.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The sign says no tasting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One representative sample. You taste it; I'll compare mine afterwards if nobody objects.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then you hold the bunch where the assistant can see it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Twist one grape off; don't pull at the whole bunch. You taste first, then I'll have something to compare.

cards.title: Recognize Me
cards.instruction: Make someone acknowledge your importance, expertise, or authority.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you cut the ribbon, please name the engineer. Bridges do not hold themselves up.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're thanking the whole council.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The council chose a colour. I corrected the load calculations. Those are separate contributions.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine. 'Thanks to our technical team.'

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One engineer. My name is on every calculation; could it reach the microphone just once?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: There's a correction to your wedding programme. 'Thanks to the buffet' should name the person who cooked it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Everyone knows you made the food.

beats.speaker: A

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you. I will say my surname once. Please repeat that version into the microphone.

cards.title: Choose Me
cards.instruction: Make yourself the choice over another person, plan, or obligation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Come to my birthday instead. I've cleared a proper dance floor; you can't turn safely between concert seats.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've already bought tickets. My friend wants dancing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then bring her here. Dancing needs space for feet, not just a speaker. I'll set two extra places.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She'll come straight from work in high heels.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll lend her flat shoes and check the fit. Shall I count you both in before I have to explain the difference between a dance floor and an aisle again?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Take me as the expedition photographer, not Martin. A sponsor needs usable pictures, not just lovely dunes.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Martin won an award for his desert photographs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For landscapes. Your sponsor wants people using the equipment. I'll frame the flask where the logo can be read.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They want the logo in every picture.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then it faces the lens, not the sun. Give me the brief; we'll settle the difference before anyone packs a camera.
